intro: IEC 104 lets an RTU in a substation or power plant report to the control room over a normal IP network. The RTU (remote terminal unit) is the box that collects the site's signals. In the control room, SCADA (the supervisory computer system) receives them. Every value has an address (the IOA: information object address), a type, and a reason it was sent. The RTU answers when asked, and speaks up by itself when something changes.
plain: IEC 104 lets a control room watch and control power stations far away, over a computer network. A box at each station reports what it sees, like a guard checking in by radio. When the control room asks, the box reads out every value it has. When something changes, such as a switch opening, it calls in at once and says exactly when it happened.

connect.title: Open the connection
connect.text: SCADA opens a TCP connection (a reliable link between two computers) to the RTU on port 2404. Nothing else happens yet.

start.title: Start data transfer
start.text: No data flows until SCADA sends STARTDT (start data transfer). The RTU confirms with STARTDT con.

ask.title: Ask for everything
ask.text: SCADA sends a general interrogation: a request for the current value of every point (every signal) the RTU has.

values.title: Values arrive
values.text: The RTU sends its measurements and the state of breaker CB-1, the switch that connects or cuts the line. Then it says it is done. Now SCADA knows the state of the whole plant.

ack.title: Confirm receipt
ack.text: SCADA sends an acknowledgment ("got it") for the frames (messages) it received. Without one, the RTU stops sending after 12 unconfirmed frames.

trip.title: A breaker trips
trip.text: Breaker CB-1 trips: it opens by itself, for example to cut off a fault. Nobody asked, but the RTU sends the change at once, with the time it happened.

frames.tcp: Open a TCP connection to port 2404

notes.tcp: Plain TCP, no IEC 104 bytes yet. The RTU accepts the connection and waits.

len4.name: Length
len4.note: 4 bytes follow: only the control field.

startdt-act.name: Control · U-frame
startdt-act.note: 0x07 is STARTDT act: a request to start data transfer.

startdt-con.name: Control · U-frame
startdt-con.note: 0x0B is STARTDT con: the confirmation. The RTU agrees.

i-0-0.name: Control · I-frame
i-0-0.note: Send number 0: SCADA's first numbered frame. Receive number 0: it has received none yet.

i-0-1.name: Control · I-frame
i-0-1.note: Send number 0, receive number 1: "I got your frame 0". Numbers are shifted one bit to the left, so 1 is sent as 02.

i-1-1.name: Control · I-frame
i-1-1.note: Send number 1: the RTU's next frame. Receive number 1: still "I got your frame 0".

s-4.name: Control · S-frame
s-4.note: 0x01 marks an S-frame: an acknowledgment only, with no data. Receive number 4 (sent as 08): "I have your frames 0 to 3".

type100.name: Type 100
type100.note: C_IC_NA_1: the interrogation command, a request for all values.

type13.name: Type 13
type13.note: M_ME_NC_1: a measured value as a 32-bit float.

type3.name: Type 3
type3.note: M_DP_NA_1: a double point, a state held in 2 bits, used for breakers and switches.

type31.name: Type 31
type31.note: M_DP_TB_1: a double point with a time tag that says when it changed.

vsq1.name: Count
vsq1.note: One information object: one value with its address.

vsq2.name: Count
vsq2.note: Two objects, each with its own address.

cot6.name: Cause 6
cot6.note: Activation: a command is being started. The second byte is the originator address (which master sent it), 0 here.

cot7.name: Cause 7
cot7.note: Activation confirmed: the RTU accepted the command.

cot10.name: Cause 10
cot10.note: Activation finished: the answer is complete.

cot20.name: Cause 20
cot20.note: Sent as part of the answer to the station interrogation.

cot3.name: Cause 3
cot3.note: Spontaneous: the value changed, nobody asked.

ca.name: Common address
ca.note: The station's address: 1. Two bytes, low byte first.

ioa0.name: IOA 0
ioa0.note: The command is for the whole station, not one point.

ioa1001.name: IOA 1001
ioa1001.note: The address of active power: 0x0003E9, low byte first.

qoi20.name: QOI 20
qoi20.note: The qualifier of the interrogation. 20 means station interrogation: every group of points.

qds.name: Quality
qds.note: Good: no flag (such as invalid or blocked) is set.

diq-on.name: State 2
diq-on.note: On: the breaker is closed. 1 is off; 0 and 3 mean moving or faulty.

cp56.name: CP56Time2a
cp56.note: A 7-byte time stamp: 7.280 s, 41 min, 10 h, Thursday 12 November (20)26. There is no time zone in it.

n-dir.name: M · monitor direction
n-dir.note: From the station to the control room. C would mean the control direction: a command from the control room.

n-dp.name: DP · double point
n-dp.note: Two bits for a switch: 01 open, 10 closed. 00 and 11 mean it is between the two, or its contacts disagree.

n-tb.name: TB · time tag
n-tb.note: With a time tag: B is the 7-byte CP56Time2a. IEC 101 also had TA, a 3-byte time; NA means no time.

n-1.note: Every type name in IEC 101 and 104 ends with 1; it tells nothing more.

facts.frames: I: data · S: acknowledge · U: control

tips: Both sides must agree on the address sizes: common address 2 bytes, IOA 3 bytes. A mismatch gives no error: the values are simply read wrong.
Time tags carry no time zone, only a summer-time bit. Agree on UTC or local time before you go live.
Acknowledge at least every 8 frames (w). After 12 unconfirmed frames (k), the RTU stops sending.

playground.encoder: Type a value and see the four bytes an IEC 104 float travels as. IEC 104 sends them low byte first (DCBA).
playground.file: The RTU's point list: what each address means. SCADA needs the same list, or it cannot read the values.
playground.common-address: The station's address. It is in every frame.
playground.ioa: The information object address: one per signal.
playground.type: How the value travels: a float, with no time tag.
playground.scale: A value sent as a float needs no scaling. Normalized and scaled types do.
playground.double: A double point: 2 bits for on, off, moving and faulty.
playground.spontaneous: When it changes, it is sent at once with a time tag.
